calls.headline: Debt outflows push the pound to 54.76 despite an IMF staff deal
calls.body: The central bank's dollar rate rose to EGP 54.63 buy and 54.76 sell by Wednesday's close, from 54.17 and 54.31 that morning, as foreigners sold a net $576m of Egyptian government debt on Tuesday and $87m on Wednesday, after buying $842.2m the week before (Al-Ain, citing EGX data; EnterpriseAM). The same day Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly said Egypt and the IMF had reached a staff-level agreement on the eighth and final review, which would unlock about $2.3bn once the board approves before the program expires on December 15 (Akhbar El-Youm, CairoScene). The EGX30 fell 0.68% to 50,538.70 on EGP 6.2bn of turnover, with 160 stocks down and 37 up (Al-Raees, Youm7).
calls.view: The outflow is the Fed, not Egypt: third-quarter US growth revised to 4.3% and core PCE at 3.3% made a December 9 hike near certain, and every hike narrows what one-year bills at 26.16% pay a dollar investor. The IMF deal and the canal's recovery cap the damage; the desk expects the dollar to stay below EGP 56.50 through the central bank's December 17 meeting, with the pound drifting rather than breaking. The EGX30 keeps its 48,000–53,000 range. Medium confidence.
calls.wrong: The central bank's dollar rate closes above EGP 56.50 before December 17, or the IMF board delays the review.

calls.headline: Maersk tells Sisi it will bring its full network back through Suez
calls.line: The world's second-largest container line returning in full is the canal's biggest step back toward pre-crisis dollars.
calls.body: Maersk chief executive Vincent Clerc told President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi on Wednesday that its sailings through the canal have resumed and its full network will return to the Red Sea route in the coming months (Daily News Egypt, Egypt Today); in October the group expected all its services back by March 2027 (Arab Finance). The canal earned $593m from 1,194 ships in November 1–24, against $295m a year earlier, while traffic is still about half its pre-crisis 70 to 80 ships a day (Suez Canal Authority via DNE Africa).
calls.view: A steady dollar stream for the pound over 2027 rather than a jump this month: no date was given, and the Houthis' strikes on Saudi Red Sea ports on the same day are the risk that could send carriers back around Africa. Alexandria Containers gains most directly from more Mediterranean calls. Medium confidence.
calls.wrong: Maersk or its Gemini partner Hapag-Lloyd suspends Suez sailings again before the end of January.

calls.headline: Houthi strikes on Saudi ports lift Brent 3.5% to $94.61
calls.line: Dearer oil raises Egypt's fuel import bill and puts the Red Sea route back at risk.
calls.body: The Houthis claimed strikes on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery and the Red Sea ports of Jeddah and Jazan on Wednesday (Al Jazeera, Middle East Eye), and Brent settled up $3.21, or 3.5%, at $94.61 (Nation Thailand, Markets.com). It rose for a third session on Thursday, above $95, before Sunday's OPEC+ meeting on 2027 output (ING).
calls.view: Bad for the pound twice over: every $10 on Brent adds to a fuel and LNG import bill already behind a September trade deficit of $5.3bn, and attacks on Red Sea ports are what kept shipping lines away from Suez. Refiners such as Alexandria Mineral Oils gain on margins only if product prices follow; the desk does not expect OPEC+ to cut on Sunday. Low confidence on the oil price itself.
calls.notice: The strikes on Jeddah and Jazan are the Houthis' claim; Saudi Arabia has not confirmed damage.

calls.headline: Orascom Construction falls 2.8% to its lowest since August as the OCI deal closes
calls.line: 97.2m new shares reach OCI's holders around December 8, and some of them may sell.
calls.body: Orascom Construction completed its combination with OCI on Wednesday, issuing 97,201,359 new shares, about 47% of the enlarged group, lifting its share count to 207.4m from 110.2m (EnterpriseAM, Forbes Middle East, TipRanks). OCI shares last trade on November 26 with a record date of November 30. The stock fell 2.8% to EGP 763.00, its lowest since August.
calls.view: Supply, not the business: the backlog of $11.6bn, $4.8bn of it in the US, is unchanged, but holders of OCI who never chose an Egypt-listed builder receive the shares before December 8, and index weights adjust. The desk drops its EGP 860–900 projection, broken when the stock closed below EGP 780, and expects selling to weigh until the new shares are in holders' accounts. Low confidence.
calls.wrong: The stock closes back above EGP 830 before December 8.

calls.headline: AI stocks claw back a 4.6% Nasdaq plunge as credit fears linger
calls.body: The Nasdaq Composite fell as much as 4.6% early on Wednesday and closed down 0.62% at 23,585.80; the S&P 500 lost 0.25% to 7,182.78 after being down 3.2%, while the Dow rose 0.33% (Reuters via Yahoo Finance, Anadolu). Nvidia fell 8.5% intraday to a fresh low before closing 3.9% lower at $149.30, Alphabet hit a 52-week low before ending down 2.1%, and Broadcom recovered a 5.8% drop to close flat. Five-year credit default swaps on Oracle, Alphabet, SpaceX and CoreWeave hit records over two sessions, and Oracle fell 5.1% to $103.88 (Reuters).
calls.view: The buyers who turned the day are bargain hunters, not a change in the story: the market still doubts that debt-funded AI spending earns its cost, and a Fed hike on December 9 raises that cost. The desk expects the AI borrowers, Oracle first, to lag the S&P 500 into the Fed, while cash-rich names hold up better. Low confidence: a thin holiday week can swing either way.

calls.headline: Growth revised up to 4.3% and core PCE at 3.3% lock in a December hike
calls.line: Hot growth and sticky inflation leave the Fed little room to wait.
calls.body: Third-quarter growth was revised up to an annualized 4.3% from 3.4%, against a 3.5% forecast, and core PCE rose 0.3% in October for an annual 3.3%, with headline PCE at 3.8% (Kotak Neo, Anadolu). Futures priced a December 9 hike as near certain, and Deutsche Bank expects three, in December, January and March, to a midpoint of 4.625% (EnterpriseAM). The 10-year Treasury yield closed at 4.85%.
calls.view: A hike is priced; the risk now is the path. If the Fed signals more, as Deutsche Bank expects, long-duration growth stocks and housing take the hit, and the dollar's strength squeezes emerging markets such as Egypt. Medium confidence.
calls.wrong: The Fed holds rates on December 9.

calls.headline: Washington proposes Section 301 tariffs on 14 trading partners, China included
calls.line: Milder than feared, Asia's markets said on Thursday, but another weight on margins.
calls.body: The US Trade Representative proposed tariffs of 15% to 40% under Section 301 on 14 trading partners on Wednesday, after the Supreme Court's February ruling against earlier duties (Sandler, Travis & Rosenberg, BBC). Asian markets rebounded on Thursday as the plan proved milder than feared, with the Nikkei and the Kospi up about 1.8% and the Hang Seng 1.3% (Business Times).
calls.view: A slow-moving risk rather than a shock: proposals go through hearings before they apply, which gives importers time. Retailers with large sourcing abroad and hardware makers carry the most exposure; HP's downgrade by HSBC cited tariffs. Low confidence.
calls.wrong: The S&P 500 closes above 7,400 before the end of December.

calls.headline: Nvidia halts AI server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries
calls.line: A license bottleneck on one of its fastest-growing regions.
calls.body: Nvidia told manufacturing partners including Dell and Supermicro to hold pending AI-server orders for Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia under US export rules that took effect last week, the Financial Times reported (via Yahoo Malaysia and The National).
calls.view: Deferred revenue rather than lost revenue if licenses come, but it lands while the stock is 20% down this year and investors already question its customers' financing. The desk expects Nvidia to lag the Nasdaq until the licenses are clear. Low confidence.
calls.notice: Reported by the Financial Times and relayed by other outlets; Nvidia has not commented.

calls.headline: Meta rises 3.4% against the tape on talks to end Amazon's Muse block
calls.line: A deal would reopen Amazon's store to Meta's shopping agent.
calls.body: Amazon and Meta have held repeated talks on connecting Meta's Muse AI agent to Amazon's store and ending a blockade imposed two months ago, with search results and advertising the main issues, Fortune reported on Wednesday; advertising is a $68.6bn business for Amazon. Meta rose 3.4% to $609.89 while Amazon fell 3.1% to $244.43.
calls.view: A small, real channel for Meta, and a question for Amazon's ad business if agents bypass its sponsored listings. Neither moves on it alone; Amazon's fall was the AI-spending selloff. Low confidence.
calls.wrong: Amazon and Meta say the talks have ended without a deal.
calls.notice: The talks are reported by one outlet (Fortune); the view does not rely on a deal.

view.headline: The IMF and Suez hold the dollar below EGP 56.50
view.body: The pound gave back 0.8% on Wednesday as foreigners sold $663m of debt in two days, but the IMF staff deal, a canal earning double last year's dollars and record remittances should keep the dollar below EGP 56.50 through the December 17 meeting. The risk is a Fed that hikes and signals more: one-year bills at 26.16% would then need to rise to hold foreign money.
